sources.title: Structured interview note preserving linked-list reorder constraints
Tagged linked-list reorder question and canonical ownership

claims.text: The source preserves high-efficiency in-place linked-list reordering with O(1) extra-space requirement, but not one exact output permutation or API.

Under the explicitly declared L0,Ln,L1,Ln-1 reference contract, the exact candidate preserves the original node identity set, remains acyclic and matches the independent identity-order oracle across exhaustive lengths and seeded random lists.

validation.command: independent node-identity topology validation of exact Java candidate
validation.reported_stdout: PASS identity-lengths=0..512 seeded-random=25000 duplicate-values=identity-checked node-set=preserved cycle=none reference-order=exact

boundary_tests.case: all list lengths 0 through 512 with distinct node identities and duplicate-capable values
boundary_tests.expected: same node identity set, no cycle, exact L0,Ln,L1,Ln-1 reference identity order

boundary_tests.case: 25,000 seeded random lists up to length 599
boundary_tests.expected: reference identity order exact, no lost/new nodes, no cycle regardless of duplicate values
identity order a,d,b,c proves correctness does not rely on value uniqueness

findings: The source preserves in-place linked-list reordering with O(1) extra-space requirement but does not preserve the exact target ordering or API; the candidate correctly labels L0,Ln,L1,Ln-1 as a reference contract.
Under that explicit reference contract, midpoint split, physical disconnection, in-place second-half reversal and alternating merge form a coherent O(n)-time/O(1)-extra-space pointer algorithm.
Independent validation compares actual node identities rather than node values, proving that duplicate values cannot mask node loss, duplication, substitution or wrong topology.
Lengths 0 through 512 plus 25,000 seeded random lists preserve exactly the original node identity set, produce no cycle and match the independent reference identity order.
The answer explains why stack/array and recursive approaches violate the strict O(1) extra-space source constraint and calls out the source ambiguity instead of inventing a unique original order.
